newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says freedom as vital as air to Russians.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says freedom as vital as air to Russians.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, marking Russia's independence day holiday on Thursday, said freedom had became as vital as air for Russians, but acknowledged popular dissatisfaction with economic hardship.

"In just seven years Russia has made a huge leap forward, we have chosen freedom and democracy, and more than once have defended our choice with honour," Yeltsin told a state reception in televised remarks.
"Freedom has become transparent to Russians as air, but it has also become as vital as air."
In a televised address marking the Russia Day national holiday, Yeltsin also told Russians that their country was moving forward.
"I know how many justified grudges people have against...the authorities," Yeltsin said.

"Despite the costs and difficulties of the transitional period, Russia is moving forward -- forward along the road of real political and economic transformations and, in doing this, overtaking many of its neighbours."

On this day in 1990, the Russian parliament chaired by Yeltsin proclaimed the sovereignty of the biggest Soviet republic in a step which the president's opponents say ultimately led to the collapse of the Soviet Union in late 1991.
The Russian navy's St Andrew's flag was raised on Thursday on the ships of the Black Sea Fleet in its home base of Sevastopol on the Ukraine's Crimean peninsula.
That became possible after Russia and Ukraine resolved a long-running dispute over ownership of the former Soviet fleet.
"It is symbolic that it was on this day, June 12, that Russian St Andrew's flag was raised on the ships of the Black Sea Fleet," Yeltsin said in his television address.

"It is a symbol of the pride, honour and power of the Russian state and it is one more proof that we have no problems that we cannot solve. Russia is establishing itself firmly on its feet," he added.
